issues.what: the moon sits about 2px right and 3px down of the target relative to the star field, and its lit face is brighter and softer, so crater rims and the terminator read less sharp
issues.fix: move the moon up and left onto the target and restore crater contrast without lifting the lit face

issues.where: panels G and I, the lit limb and the rings
issues.what: the outer cyan limb glow falls off sooner and the ring arcs are dimmer and softer than the target, so the limb and rings lose presence
issues.fix: widen the limb glow back out into space and raise ring brightness and edge contrast to the target

issues.where: right limb and lower right rings
issues.what: the outer atmospheric haze is narrower and dimmer than the target, and the ring filaments are softer and slightly darker
issues.fix: extend and lift the limb falloff and sharpen the ring arcs back to the target brightness

issues.where: planet disc, storm and cloud bands
issues.what: the same shot, but fine cloud edges are softer and the disc is about 2px right and 1px up of the target while the star and glare stay put
issues.fix: shift the planet back onto the target and restore high-frequency cloud detail

issues.where: panels A, E, F and H, cloud decks
issues.what: same crops and identical labels, but the panels do not share one registration (about 3px right and 1px up on the storm and limb panels, about 1px on the limb and ring panels) and cloud edges are softer
issues.fix: register every panel to the target and put the fine cloud detail back

issues.what: same shot and same star field, but the frame is about one RGB level brighter and cloud and squall edges are softer, with the storm and cloud front about 2px right of the target
issues.fix: drop the exposure a step, shift the planet back, and restore edge detail

issues.what: same crops and identical labels, each about one RGB level brighter and slightly soft; most panels sit about 4px right and 1px down of the target while the star-field panels F and C do not
issues.fix: match the target exposure, register each panel, and restore the fine cloud edges
